Kafka uses logs to record a continuous stream of events.
Properties:
Kafka organizes logs/events into topics.
Each topic is like a table in an RDBMS, holding related event logs.

content.text: Monitoring the speed of train A2B:

items: 4-hour journey × 60 mins = 240 logs/day
50 trains → 87,600 × 50 = ~4.3 million logs/year
A2B_SPEED: General logs of train A2B.
A2B_SPEED_DEC_25_2022: Filtered logs for a specific day.
Kafka splits topics into partitions to:
Each partition is an ordered, immutable sequence of messages.
Kafka messages are typically in Key-Value format.
Messages with the same key go to the same partition – maintains order.
Distributed round-robin across all partitions – no guaranteed order.
Kafka provides the ConsumerRecord<K,V> class to access both:
Key
Value
Timestamp
Partition
Offset
Topic name
Single Project: Includes both Kafka Producer and Consumer.
Events are modeled as key-value pairs.
Requires a Kafka instance running locally.
